The rule is built and its tests pass; four things the pages leave open, each with what the build does meanwhile. (1) The route. 01b:77-78 says seeing a closed pull request wants 'a read of closed pull requests' in the writer's guard, GET only, and points at L-AM2 in 07; 07's L-AM2 names one route, GET commits/<sha>/pulls. As I read GitHub's REST page for that route (documentation, never observed live for a closed one), a commit that is not on the default branch lists its open pull requests and the merged one, so a pull request closed unmerged from brain/c/<id> is not in that answer, and a candidate whose branch a person deleted has no commit to ask by. The build adds a second read, by the branch's name: GET pulls?state=closed&head=<owner>:<branch>&base=brain/integration&per_page=100, taken by the guard in that one spelling for branches under brain/ of the configured repository (tests.test_write.ClosedPulls). It is GET only, as 01b:78 says, but it is a route no page names and the first with a query string. Asked: the page naming the route, or saying that the commit's list is the one meant. Nothing of it was observed live: the rehearsal toy has had no closed pull request of a candidate's branch. (2) Who closed it. 01b:77 says the writer closes no pull request, 'the one who closes is a person'. 25a deletes every brain/ branch before a new genesis, and as I read GitHub's documentation (a hypothesis, not observed) deleting the head branch of an open pull request closes that pull request. Such a pull request would then be closed by the deletion, not by a person's decision about the fix, and the build cannot tell the two apart: it reads state and merged_at, not who closed or when. (3) Between which geneses. 26p:76-80 bounds a used id by 'since the last genesis'; 01b:75-80 gives pull_closed no such bound. The build follows the sentence as written: any pull request from brain/c/<id> into brain/integration that is closed and unmerged ends the candidate of that id, also one closed before the last genesis, although the id may be used again after it (26p). With (2) this could refuse, after a new genesis, every id that had an open pull request at the deletion. Asked: whether pull_closed counts only pull requests opened since the last genesis (the ledger has no row for a pull request that never merged, so the bound would need a time or a number to compare), or every one. (4) The genesis cycle and the base. The genesis cycle's merge is landed by the activation after it created brain/integration; a refusal there, pull_closed too, is the activation's failed write (28:57), not 'that id only, the cycle goes on'. Not judged against 01b and held by no test (the same holds for branch_differs there, stated in loop.job). The base is not named by 01b: the build reads pull requests into brain/integration only, the one base a fix has (01b:40-41). What the build promises is in target/write.py 'Closed pull' and target/land.py; what it does not: anything about a list longer than one page beyond refusing a full page with no closed unmerged item (an API error, the cycle's outage), and a pull request from a fork's branch of the same name, told apart only by GitHub's head filter. Nothing is red.
